notes: All cases are derived from released numerical summaries; no videos or new rollouts are claimed.

cases.title: A high-retention W3 operating point
cases.observation: W3 retains 556/600 successes (92.7%), compared with 586/600 (97.7%) at W4.
cases.interpretation: Use as a quality/storage reference; the 5.0-point difference is descriptive, not a significance test.

cases.title: Spatial: a useful W2.5 regime
cases.interpretation: The pooled 70.5% average hides meaningful differences between suites.

cases.title: Object: retention at lower bitwidth
cases.observation: Object achieves 150/150 at W3 and W2.5, and 138/150 (92.0%) at W2.
cases.interpretation: A strong Object score does not imply the same retention on other suites.

cases.title: Goal: an explicit low-bit failure case
cases.observation: Goal falls from 125/150 at W3 to 26/150 at W2.5, 2/150 at W2, and 0/150 at W1.5*.
cases.interpretation: Inspect failures as well as successes when choosing a budget.

cases.title: Long: guided allocation versus random
cases.observation: Guided W2.5 reaches 127/150 successes (84.7%); calibrated random W2.5 reaches 0/150.
cases.interpretation: Both configurations include calibration; this comparison does not isolate calibration itself.

cases.title: The full lambda sweep
cases.observation: Success counts are 395, 381, 423, 406, and 400 out of 600 for lambda=0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1.
cases.interpretation: The tested default lambda=0.5 is 4.7 percentage points above lambda=0 after rounding.

cases.title: An overall winner is not a suite-wise winner
cases.observation: Lambda=0.75 reaches 30/150 on Goal versus 26/150 for lambda=0.5, while its overall total is 406/600 versus 423/600.
cases.interpretation: The best overall setting need not maximize every task family.

cases.title: Calibration cannot rescue arbitrary allocation
cases.observation: Calibrated random W2.5 reaches 49/600 (8.2%); guided W2.5 reaches 423/600 (70.5%).
cases.interpretation: This supports informed allocation within the calibrated pipeline, not an independent calibration ablation.

cases.title: Asymmetric extreme compression
cases.observation: W1.5* retains W4 vision and W1.5 language: 153/600 overall, with 58/150 Spatial versus 44/150 at W2.
cases.interpretation: W1.5* is approximately 1.75 bits across target weights; quality is not monotonic in every suite.

cases.title: Whole-model storage versus latency
cases.observation: W1.5* changes from 2.656 GB / 250.5 ms without coding to 2.534 GB / 310.4 ms with grouped coding.
cases.interpretation: The coded record gives 6.10x complete-model compression and 3.537 GB peak allocation. Coding adds 59.9 ms.

cases.title: Minimum memory and fast decoding are different points
cases.observation: W1.5* CODEBOOK001 measures 2.784 GB / 1771.9 ms; CODEBOOK003 measures 3.537 GB / 310.4 ms.
cases.interpretation: Do not combine the 2.784 GB minimum with the 310.4 ms latency.

cases.title: Coding overhead depends on the configuration
cases.observation: The grouped-coded W2.5 record takes 473.9 ms; the grouped-coded W1.5* record takes 310.4 ms.
cases.interpretation: Fewer stored bits do not alone determine decoder or full model-action latency.

cases.title: From priorities to 428 matrix assignments
cases.observation: At W2.5, changing lambda from 0 to 0.5 changes W1/W2/W3/W4 counts from 54/107/189/78 to 19/150/199/60.
cases.interpretation: These are matrix counts, not parameter-weighted bit averages.
